_design: ONE model, trained ONCE on the pooled training datasets of every family, then
evaluated on each family's held-out dataset(s) (100% of their *test.csv files).
Per family, one or more datasets go into the shared TRAIN pool and the rest are
held out. Every held-out dataset has at least one same-family sibling in the pool,
and contributes zero training windows itself.
family        TRAIN pool ->            HELD OUT
ecg           MITDB          ->        SVDB
spacecraft    SMAP           ->        MSL
env_iot       CalIt2, GECCO  ->        metro, room-occupancy
industrial    GHL            ->        Genesis
server        SMD, Exathlon  ->        PSM, cicids
activity      Daphnet        ->        OPPORTUNITY
TRAIN pool (8) : MITDB, SMAP, CalIt2, GECCO, GHL, SMD, Exathlon, Daphnet
HELD OUT   (8) : SVDB, MSL, metro, room-occupancy, Genesis, PSM, cicids, OPPORTUNITY
'holdout' is a LIST: a family may hold out more than one dataset (env_iot, server).
Each held-out dataset becomes one row in the deliverable table, credited to that
family's whole train list as its same-family sibling(s).
This is F2A's protocol (one jointly fine-tuned model, evaluated on datasets excluded
from training) with the confound removed: sibling coverage is guaranteed by design.
SAMPLER: the pool is drawn with the 1.5-level hierarchical sampler --
level 1    dataset ~ Uniform(K)                 K = 8 train datasets
level 1.5  file    ~ dissimilarity weight w_f   (multi-file train datasets only)
level 2    kind    ~ Bernoulli(P_ANOM=1/3)      2:1 normal:anomalous
level 3    window  ~ count-weighted within (dataset, file, kind)
Level 1.5 up-weights train files that are dissimilar to their dataset's other files,
so a dataset's budget is spent across its distinct PATTERNS rather than its longest
recordings. It is a no-op on single-file train datasets (CalIt2, GECCO).
TRADE-OFF, state it in the writeup: a single pooled model cannot attribute a gain on
SVDB to MITDB specifically -- the model also saw SMAP, SMD, GHL and the rest. It
answers 'does a family-sibling-covered pool transfer to unseen datasets', not 'which
sibling did the work'. Per-family attribution needs one model per family (6 runs);
the machinery supports it via  python make_folds.py --per_family.
tier 1 = defensible. tier 2 = UNDERPOWERED, report separately (see 'caveat').

ecg.note: Both 2-lead ECG, F=3, ~13% anomalous, same anomaly semantics (arrhythmic beats). The flagship.

spacecraft.note: Both NASA telemetry. F differs (SMAP 26 / MSL 56); most channels are one-hot command flags.

env_iot.caveat: Both held-out sets are anomaly-sparse (metro ~31 anomalous timesteps; room-occupancy small). VUS-PR is noise-dominated -- a bad number does NOT mean transfer failed. CalIt2 in the train pool is itself anomaly-sparse (~138 steps), so its level-3 anomalous branch is thin.
env_iot.note: Weakest grouping: door counts (CalIt2) + water quality (GECCO) -> freeway traffic (metro) + room CO2 (room-occupancy) is 'has sensors', not one domain.

industrial.caveat: Genesis has ~28 anomalous timesteps TOTAL (0.30% of 9332). VUS-PR is noise-dominated; a bad number does NOT mean transfer failed.
industrial.note: Reverse direction (train on Genesis) is not viable -- far too few anomaly windows.

server.caveat: cicids* is a stretch of 'server': it is network intrusion traffic, not host/cloud metrics. Report its row with that asterisk -- a null there may be sub-domain mismatch, not failed transfer. PSM (anomaly-dense, ~32%) is the clean server-family holdout.
server.note: PSM held out: 1 file, well-conditioned VUS-PR. cicids held out: 6 files, network flows.

activity.note: Same sensor modality (body-worn IMU) but DIFFERENT anomaly semantics (freezing-of-gait vs activity transition). A null result here is ambiguous between domain mismatch and label mismatch.

excluded_singletons._comment: One-dataset families -- no sibling, so same-family transfer is undefined. Excluded from BOTH pool and held-out set. (cicids was here before; it now serves as a server-family holdout with an asterisk, see server.caveat.)
